design:
Tier 1: validators at create doors and a test, no schema, no migration, no route move, no UI bundle.

D1. The words live in a Hub-only module (hub/hub/route_words.py), each with the route it loses to, and are checked only where an agent row or a task is created. Not in _RESERVED_AGENT_NAMES or the CLI's RESERVED_AGENT_NAMES: those are checked at every use site, so an agent already named settings would stop running (CLAUDE.md; overhaul-route-shadow-names).
D2. A session sync refuses a route word only for an agent row it would add; a name already in the project syncs as before. Follows from D1.
D3. One task-id check beside _TASK_ID_RE, called by TaskCreate and AgentTaskCreate, so the agent door answers 422 and not a 500 from re-validation inside its handler (agent_actions.py:245); jobs.py:917's initial tasks already answer 422 on a TaskCreate error.
D4. Words are compared case-insensitively, as the reserved names are (worktrees.py:153), although the route match itself is exact. Rejected: refusing only the exact lowercase word (Settings would be accepted beside a refused settings, two rules for one list). (night-1010-8)
D5. The route walk matches whole paths (shared method, equal depth, every segment equal or literal-vs-parameter) and keys on the match, not on parameter names; Hub-minted parameters (runner_id; full_path, the UI catch-all) are an explicit allowlist in the test.
D6. Routes answer: POST /agents and /agents/request 400 with the sentence (the Add-agent dialog renders detail as text, agents.py:690-692); session sync 400; task doors 422 naming id.

problem: Re-walked on today's tree from the built app's app.routes (whole-path match, shared method, equal depth): GET /worktrees/conflicts is registered before GET /worktrees/{agent}; GET /queue/settings before GET /queue/{agent}; GET /agent/sessions/{agent} before GET /agent/{agent}/chat and /agent/{agent}/conversations (a path /agent/sessions/chat matches both, the earlier wins); GET /tasks/board and /tasks/boards before GET /tasks/{task_id}. The UI reads every victim route (api/queue.ts, api/workspace.ts, api/agentChat.ts, the task drawer). AGENT_NAME_RE accepts all three agent words and _TASK_ID_RE (schemas/tasks.py:17) both task words, so an operator or an agent can create a resource whose own panel shows some other resource's answer. F248 measured the first row (GET /worktrees/conflicts answers 200 [] for an agent named conflicts). The shared reserved set (worktrees.py:73-79, constants.py:79) cannot take these words: validate_agent_name is checked at every use site (agent_roster.py:36, agent_trigger.py:886, worktrees.py:163-227), so an agent that already holds one would stop running.

requirements.rationale: overhaul-route-shadow-names (F248): refuse at creation only, Hub-only, so an existing agent that holds the word is not stopped by a check at every use site.
requirements.statement: Every Hub door that creates an agent row MUST refuse a name that a route registered before the agent's own routes would answer for (today conflicts, settings and sessions, compared case-insensitively), with a sentence naming that route; no check outside agent creation MUST refuse such a name.

requirements.rationale: AgentTaskCreate re-validates through TaskCreate inside the handler (agent_actions.py:245); a TaskCreate-only check would answer 500 at the agent door.
requirements.statement: Creating a task through the operator door, the agent door or a loop's initial tasks MUST refuse an id that a route registered before GET /tasks/{task_id} would answer for (today board and boards, case-insensitively) with a 422 naming id, never a 500.

requirements.rationale: The queue and sessions collisions existed when F248 was filed and nobody saw them; a list is only durable if the route table checks it.
requirements.statement: The Hub's tests MUST fail, naming the route and the word, when a route with a fixed segment is registered before a route whose caller-named parameter at that segment it matches over the whole path, unless the word is refused for that parameter's resource or the parameter is Hub-minted (runner_id, the UI catch-all full_path).

in_scope: A Hub-only list of route words, each with the route it loses to, refused when an agent row is created: POST /agents (agents.py:694), POST /agents/request (agents.py:2660), and a session sync that adds a new agent row (session_sync.py:113-133)

Task ids board and boards refused by one shared check called from TaskCreate (schemas/tasks.py:80) and AgentTaskCreate (agent_actions.py:138), so both doors and a loop's initial tasks answer 422 naming id
A Hub test that walks app.routes and fails when a literal route shadows a caller-named parameter whose word is not refused
non_goals: The shared RESERVED_AGENT_NAMES / _RESERVED_AGENT_NAMES sets and the CLI's is_valid_agent_name: unchanged
Moving or reordering routes; no UI bundle
Renaming or refusing an agent or task that already holds one of the words: it keeps running, still unreadable at the shadowed route

summary: FastAPI matches routes in declaration order, so a fixed word declared before a caller-named parameter at the same place in the address claims that word: a resource created under it exists, is listed, and can never be read at its own address. Five words collide today: agent names conflicts, settings and sessions, and task ids board and boards. The operator decided (overhaul-route-shadow-names, F248) to refuse those words when an agent or task is created, at the Hub only, not by widening the shared reserved-name set, and to let a route-table test catch the next collision. Re-authored from openspec change a-name-a-caller-chooses-reaches-its-own-resource.
